title: Loyalty program → monthly spend
teaser: Big spenders were pushed to join; points only exist after joining.
question: Does joining our loyalty program actually raise monthly spend?
ask: I need the average effect across all customers, and whether newer customers gain more.

outcome.name: monthly_spend
outcome.label: Monthly spend
outcome.meaning: spend in the month after the launch window ($)
outcome.recorded: the month after the launch window

variables.name: tenure_months
variables.label: Months as a customer
variables.recorded: at the start of the period

variables.name: prior_quarter_spend
variables.label: Spend last quarter
variables.meaning: total spend in the quarter before launch ($)

hidden.name: U_engaged
hidden.label: how engaged the customer already is

hidden.name: U_engaged_strong
hidden.label: store managers enrolling their 'regulars' by hand

post_treatment.name: survey_satisfaction
post_treatment.label: Satisfaction score
post_treatment.meaning: satisfaction score from the post-launch survey (0-10)

negative_control.name: spend_before_launch_week
negative_control.label: Spend in the week before launch
negative_control.meaning: spend in the week before the program launched ($)

notes.text: Joining was voluntary. Marketing pushed the program harder in cities.
Marketing also targeted people who already spent a lot.
Only members can earn and redeem points.
Store managers personally signed up their regulars, but nobody recorded who those regulars were.

traps.name: Post-treatment column
traps.text: points_redeemed only exists after joining; controlling for it wrecks the estimate.

traps.name: Targeting on past spend
traps.text: Big spenders were pushed to join; leaving prior spend out inflates the effect.

traps.name: Collider
traps.text: Satisfaction is caused by both joining and spending; controlling for it biases the answer.

traps.name: Unrecorded driver
traps.text: Managers enrolled their regulars by hand; nothing recorded captures it, so the effect can't be pinned down.
